contribution_types.label: Algorithms / General
contribution_types.scope: A new method, model or algorithm in computer vision; also the default and boundary category.
contribution_types.quote: Select this category if your paper’s main contribution is a new method, model, algorithm, etc. in computer vision or related areas.

contribution_types.label: Theory / Foundational
contribution_types.scope: Theoretical understanding, formal analysis or foundational principles; strong empirical results are welcome but not required.
contribution_types.quote: Select this category if your paper primarily advances theoretical understanding, formal analysis, or foundational principles of computer vision or machine learning.

contribution_types.label: Applied / Systems
contribution_types.scope: A practical system, real-world deployment, large-scale implementation or engineering solution.
contribution_types.quote: Select this category if your main contribution is a practical system, real-world deployment, large-scale implementation, or engineering solution.

contribution_types.label: Datasets / Benchmarks
contribution_types.scope: A new dataset, benchmark, evaluation protocol or challenge; public release by camera-ready is required.
contribution_types.quote: Select this category if your primary contribution is a new dataset, benchmark, evaluation protocol, or challenge for the community.

contribution_types.label: Concept & Feasibility
contribution_types.scope: A novel idea, paradigm or research direction with feasibility-level validation rather than full-scale development.
contribution_types.quote: Select this category if your paper introduces a novel idea, paradigm, or research direction with feasibility-level validation rather than full-scale experimental development.

review_criteria.name: Assessment through the selected Contribution Type
review_criteria.official_explanation: Reviewers assess each paper against its declared Contribution Type; a Datasets/Benchmarks paper is not penalized for lacking a novel method.
review_criteria.quote: This attribute specifies how you should assess a paper.

review_criteria.name: Technical soundness
review_criteria.official_explanation: Accepted papers should be technically sound and contribute to the field.
review_criteria.quote: Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.

review_criteria.name: Novelty and potential impact
review_criteria.official_explanation: Novelty and impact are weighed together with reported performance.
review_criteria.quote: Rather, it is important to weigh both the novelty and potential impact of the work alongside the reported performance.

review_criteria.name: Fit to ECCV subject areas
review_criteria.official_explanation: Out-of-scope papers must be explained and redirected to better-matched venues.
review_criteria.quote: If you think the paper is out of scope for ECCV's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review.

review_criteria.name: Reproducibility and code
review_criteria.official_explanation: Code submission is encouraged and reviewers may optionally check it confidentially.
review_criteria.quote: To improve reproducibility in AI research, we highly encourage authors to voluntarily submit their code as part of supplementary material, especially if they plan to release it upon acceptance.

review_criteria.name: Honest discussion of limitations
review_criteria.official_explanation: An honest limitations discussion is weighed positively and cannot be the sole rejection factor.
review_criteria.quote: authors are encouraged to explicitly and honestly discuss limitations.

review_criteria.name: Ethics and ethical concerns
review_criteria.official_explanation: Papers using personal or human-subject data need IRB clearance or a description of the ethical principles followed.
review_criteria.quote: If a paper is using personal data or data from human subjects, the authors must have an ethics clearance from an institutional review board (IRB, or equivalent) or clearly describe that ethical principles have been followed.

mandatory_policy.statement: Papers are limited to 14 pages including figures and tables in the Springer LNCS style, plus reference-only pages.
mandatory_policy.quote: Papers are limited to 14 pages, including figures and tables, in the LNCS style of Springer.

mandatory_policy.statement: Non-anonymized, non-template or over-length papers may be rejected without review.
mandatory_policy.quote: Papers that are not properly anonymized, do not use the template, or have more than 14 pages (excluding references) may be rejected without review.

mandatory_policy.statement: No substantially similar publication may be submitted elsewhere during the ECCV 2026 review period.
mandatory_policy.quote: no publication substantially similar in content has been submitted to, or will be submitted to, another conference, workshop, or journal during the review period (from March 13, 2026 until the Final Decision).

mandatory_policy.statement: ECCV 2026 does not allow LLMs or online chatbots in any part of the reviewing process.
mandatory_policy.quote: ECCV2026 does not allow the use of Large Language Models or online chatbots such as ChatGPT in any part of the reviewing process.

mandatory_policy.statement: Papers declaring the Datasets/Benchmarks contribution type must make the dataset/benchmark publicly available by camera-ready, with a stable URL in the paper.
mandatory_policy.quote: By selecting Datasets/Benchmarks as the primary contribution type, authors confirm that the proposed dataset and/or benchmark that are claimed as a contribution of the paper will be publicly available by the time of camera-ready submission
mandatory_policy.conditions: Applies only to submissions that select the Datasets/Benchmarks contribution type; failure removes the paper from the proceedings.

recommended_practice.statement: Code upload as supplementary material is encouraged but not required.
recommended_practice.quote: We encourage (but do not require) authors to upload their code as part of their supplementary material in order to help reviewers assess the quality of the work.

recommended_practice.statement: An explicit and honest limitations discussion is encouraged and weighed positively.
recommended_practice.quote: authors are encouraged to explicitly and honestly discuss limitations.

recommended_practice.statement: Authors are encouraged to discuss potential negative societal impact; omission is not a formal violation.
recommended_practice.quote: authors are encouraged to include a discussion on potential negative societal impact.

compliance_checks.requirement: Submission and supplementary material do not identify the authors.
Main paper is at most 14 pages excluding references.
The ECCV 2026 template and font are used; old templates are not accepted.
Datasets/Benchmarks papers provide a stable public URL by camera-ready.
Reviews and meta-reviews are not produced with an LLM and submissions are not uploaded to one by the program committee.

changes_from_prior_year.change: ECCV 2026 introduces author-selected Contribution Types and an accompanying Dataset Release Policy; the reviewer guidelines state that these guidelines contain changes with respect to past conferences.
ECCV 2026 uses a new template: the Submission Policies state that the template has changed since ECCV 2024 and that older templates must not be used.
ECCV 2026 strictly enforces the reviewing deadline, with desk rejection of an author-reviewer's papers for late reviews.

unknown_policies.question: Does ECCV 2026 run a separate journal or journal-to-conference track?
unknown_policies.reason: The retrieved ECCV 2026 CFP and submission policies describe a single main technical program and do not mention a journal track, so the track is recorded as "main".

unknown_policies.question: What rating scale and fields does the ECCV 2026 review form use?
unknown_policies.reason: The review form was not among the retrieved sources; only the reviewer guidelines and contribution-type guidance are available.

unknown_policies.question: Are ECCV 2026 Contribution Types tracks, and can more than one apply?
unknown_policies.reason: The author guidance answers this directly for selection (one primary type, not separate tracks), but no official secondary-type taxonomy is published, so secondary type assignment is not established.
